disclaimer: Mechanistic and epidemiological education, not a diagnosis. Relationships describe how systems generally interact in child growth; they are not claims about an individual child's cause of growth. Always interpret with the treating clinician.

domains.label: Growth signaling
domains.question: Is growth signaling broadly compatible with the observed growth?

domains.label: Growth-plate response
domains.question: Is the skeleton responding, and how much growth time remains?

domains.label: Iron & oxygen
domains.question: Are iron stores and oxygen delivery potentially limiting?

analytes.label: IGF-1
analytes.meaning: IGF-1 carries much of growth hormone's signal to bone and cartilage, supporting growth-plate cell hypertrophy and matrix expansion — not simply making more cells.
cautions: Interpret as an SDS adjusted for age, sex and ideally pubertal stage — concentrations change greatly through childhood and peak around puberty; a single universal range is misleading.
Never infer growth-hormone deficiency or sufficiency from IGF-1 alone — combine with height velocity, bone age and clinical context.
Around early puberty, interpretation is less certain when pubertal stage is unknown.

analytes.label: Vitamin D
analytes.meaning: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption and bone mineralization — part of the environment growth happens in, not a direct switch for height.
cautions: Belongs in the bone/mineral support domain, not as a direct height-growth driver.
Human evidence for a height effect is modest and not uniform across sexes.

analytes.label: Ferritin
analytes.meaning: Ferritin reflects iron stores. Low stores can reduce energy and, with anemia, may affect growth — but higher is not better.
cautions: Not a 'higher is better' marker — do not reward rising ferritin with a better score.
Interpret alongside hemoglobin and red-cell indices; ferritin is also an inflammatory marker.
Low ferritin with normal hemoglobin = reduced iron stores, NOT anemia.

analytes.label: Hemoglobin
analytes.meaning: Hemoglobin reflects oxygen-carrying capacity — a systemic-health and stamina marker.
cautions: Growth relevance of hemoglobin trends is clearest in specific disease contexts (e.g. chronic kidney disease); do not over-generalize.
Interpret with iron indices, not alone.

analytes.label: TSH
analytes.meaning: TSH is a regulator of thyroid output; thyroid hormone drives metabolic rate and skeletal maturation.
cautions: TSH alone is not a complete thyroid assessment — free T4 and growth history are needed before interpreting.
Delayed treatment of hypothyroidism can leave incomplete catch-up growth, so thyroid is a high-importance domain.

analytes.label: Free T4
analytes.meaning: Free T4 is the active thyroid hormone level; pairing it with TSH classifies thyroid status.
cautions: High TSH + low free T4 is a stronger growth-relevant pattern than high TSH with normal free T4.

relationships.mechanism: Growth hormone stimulates circulating (hepatic) and locally produced bone/cartilage IGF-1.
IGF-1 activates the IGF-1 receptor on growth-plate chondrocytes.
Downstream PI3K → AKT → mTOR drives cell survival and protein synthesis.
Downstream RAS → MAPK drives proliferation and differentiation.
IGF-1 augments chondrocyte hypertrophy and matrix expansion; loss reduces long-bone growth even with normal chondrocyte proliferation.
Cartilage matrix production and ossification produce longitudinal bone growth.
GH also promotes growth-plate chondrogenesis through IGF-independent routes — so IGF-1 cannot represent the whole GH–growth axis.
IGF signaling crosstalks with Wnt/β-catenin (osteoblast differentiation, bone formation).
IGF signaling crosstalks with BMP/TGF-β signaling.
IGF signaling crosstalks with Hedgehog/PTHrP (growth-plate maturation timing).
Vitamin D supports calcium absorption and the mineralization environment; a modest, non-uniform association with linear growth.
Iron-deficiency anemia can coexist with slower growth in young children; growth may improve after treatment. In iron-replete children the relationship is mixed.
Declining hemoglobin has tracked with worsening growth in specific disease populations (e.g. CKD); disease-specific evidence.
Thyroid hormone supports metabolic rate and skeletal maturation; untreated/late-treated hypothyroidism can permanently reduce adult stature.

pattern_rules.when: ferritin low AND hemoglobin low AND mcv low
pattern_rules.reading: Iron-deficiency pattern — worth clinician review of iron status.
Reduced iron stores without current anemia — relevance to growth possible but not certain; do not label anemia.
Thyroid pattern with stronger growth relevance — clinician review.
Different interpretation and lower certainty — free T4 and growth history needed.
Concordant low growth signaling and slow growth — a stronger reason for endocrine review.
Discordant — low IGF-1 with normal growth; investigate context (assay, puberty, nutrition) before concern.

safety_rules: Never diagnose growth-hormone deficiency from IGF-1 alone.
Never interpret TSH as a complete thyroid assessment without free T4.
Never reward increasingly high ferritin, IGF-1 or hemoglobin with a better score.
Use the reporting laboratory's pediatric reference range whenever available.
Do not recommend supplement doses or growth-hormone adjustments.
Show urgent/critical alerts only from validated laboratory-specific thresholds.
Always display interpretation confidence and what context is missing.

ruan2024.title: IGF signaling pathway in bone and cartilage development, homeostasis, and disease
ruan2024.claim: IGF ligands/receptors act on bone and cartilage via PI3K–AKT and MAPK, with crosstalk to Wnt/β-catenin, BMP/TGF-β, Hedgehog/PTH and mTOR; endocrine vs locally produced IGF-1 are distinct.

juul1994.title: Serum insulin-like growth factor-I in 1030 healthy children, adolescents, and adults: relation to age, sex, stage of puberty, testicular size, and body mass index
juul1994.claim: IGF-1 varies substantially by age, sex and pubertal stage; puberty-specific grouping reduces unexplained variation, so IGF-1 must be normalized rather than read raw.

ly2024.title: Interpreting IGF-1 in children treated with recombinant growth hormone: challenges during early puberty
ly2024.claim: Pubertal signs and sex-steroid exposure complicate IGF-1 SDS interpretation, particularly around early puberty.

kristrom2014.title: IGF-1 and growth response to adult height in a randomized GH treatment trial in short non-GH-deficient children
kristrom2014.claim: The treatment-related change in IGF-1 SDS was the strongest IGF-system variable associated with long-term adult-height response. Applies to GH-treated short children, not untreated children.
kristrom2014.scope_note: GH-treated children only — do not generalize to untreated children.

wang1999.title: Igf1 promotes longitudinal bone growth by insulin-like actions augmenting chondrocyte hypertrophy
wang1999.claim: In IGF-1-null mice, long-bone growth fell ~35% despite normal chondrocyte proliferation; the deficit was smaller hypertrophic chondrocytes — IGF-1 acts on cell hypertrophy and anabolism, not just cell number.

wu2015.title: Insulin-like growth factor-independent effects of growth hormone on growth plate chondrogenesis and longitudinal bone growth
wu2015.claim: GH promoted chondrogenesis and longitudinal growth even when local IGF-1/IGF-2 receptor effects were blocked — IGF-1 cannot represent the whole GH–growth pathway.

gilbertdiamond2010.title: Vitamin D deficiency and anthropometric indicators of adiposity in school-age children: a prospective study
gilbertdiamond2010.claim: In 479 schoolchildren (~30 mo), vitamin D deficiency was related to slower linear growth in girls (-0.6 cm/y, P=0.04) but not boys; the sex interaction was not statistically significant.
gilbertdiamond2010.scope_note: Primary endpoint was adiposity; the linear-growth finding is a secondary outcome.

soliman2009.title: Linear growth in children with iron deficiency anemia before and after treatment
soliman2009.claim: 40 young children with iron-deficiency anemia were shorter with lower growth-velocity SDS than controls; measures improved after treatment and growth velocity correlated with ferritin.

perng2013.title: Iron status and linear growth: a prospective study in school-age children
perng2013.claim: In 2,714 iron-replete schoolchildren (~30 mo), higher ferritin was associated with slower height-SDS change in boys, none in girls; hemoglobin was unrelated to growth. Ferritin is not linearly 'better when higher'.

rivkees1988.title: Long-term growth in juvenile acquired hypothyroidism: the failure to achieve normal adult stature
rivkees1988.claim: Thyroid replacement produced catch-up growth, but some children did not regain their prior trajectory or expected adult height, especially after prolonged disease.

akchurin2023.title: Longitudinal relationship between anemia and statural growth impairment in children and adolescents with nonglomerular CKD
akchurin2023.claim: In nonglomerular CKD, declining hemoglobin tracked with worsening growth even before conventional anemia thresholds.
akchurin2023.scope_note: CKD population — disease-specific, do not generalize to healthy children.
